modules.name: qdocmanagement
modules.description: QDoc management: the bounded context for quality documents (procedures, guidelines, instructions, policies) that organisations holding a quality certificate must maintain. This change covers drafting, from creating a QDoc until a version is approved; publication, employee sign-off and deletion live elsewhere or later. The root package also holds the shared notions of users, roles and organisations that every child module relies on.

modules.name: drafting
modules.description: Drafting of a QDoc: the QDoc aggregate that owns its versions, the invitations and assignments of each version, and for each version two lists of references: to its content files, stored in content management, and to its attachments, stored in the file store. The QDoc root checks every drafting invariant in one transaction, under optimistic concurrency on the whole aggregate. Its use cases create a QDoc and its versions, invite people, add and remove files, share and archive; adding a file creates it in its module and references it from the version in the same transaction. Drafting answers content management's question of who may do what with a version's content through QDocVersionAccess. Its events live in the messages submodule.

modules.name: messages
modules.description: The events drafting publishes: QDocEvent, the common notion the activity list records, and every event the QDoc aggregate raises when it changes. Kept apart from the aggregate so that activity, notifications and approval depend on these messages rather than on the aggregate itself.

modules.name: approval
modules.description: Review and approval of a version in preparation: the reviewers' "reviewed" marks and the per-approver approval of every content file and every attachment, up to the moment the version becomes approved. One VersionReview aggregate per version holds them. Its use cases read the version's people and state from drafting, each content file's revision and open comments from content management and each attachment's status from the file store. Approving a content file locks it in content management, approving an attachment locks it on the version in drafting, and the last approval marks the version approved, all in the same transaction, so every approval rule stays strongly consistent. Comments are not here: they live with the content file they are on.

modules.name: numbering
modules.description: Document numbers: the human-facing `<sequence>/<month>/<year>` identifier a QDoc receives when it is created, with the monthly per-organisation sequence, the organisation's fixed prefix and suffix, the `demo` prefix of a demo instance and the auditor suffix.

modules.name: platform
modules.description: Supporting capabilities the QDoc domain relies on but that are not drafting or approval themselves: content management for the content files and their comments, the file store for attachments and their scanning, the activity list that records everything that happens to a QDoc, and the e-mail notifications. Its submodules know nothing of the QDoc aggregate: they refer to a QDoc only by the shared QDocId, and content management asks drafting about access through its VersionAccess port.

modules.name: contentmanagement
modules.description: Content files and everything on them: the rich-text body the authors write, its revision and change history, the comments the drafting team leaves on fragments of it, and the lock an approval sets. One ContentFile aggregate per content file, so edits and comments on one file never contend with another file. The module knows nothing of QDocs beyond the QDoc and version a file belongs to: its own use cases ask drafting who may see, edit, comment on or close comments on a version's content through the VersionAccess port, which drafting implements.

modules.name: filestore
modules.description: The store of attachments: the uploaded PDF files, their quarantine until the scanner has checked them for malware and unacceptable content, and the verdict that makes them active or rejected. An attachment is immutable once stored, so the same stored attachment can belong to several versions of a QDoc. Scanning lives here: the port to the scanner and the reaction to its verdict. Attachment size limits are undecided pending research and are not checked yet.

modules.name: activity
modules.description: The activity list of a QDoc: the append-only audit trail of everything that happened to it, recorded from the QDoc's events in the same transaction as the change, and marking which actions the system took rather than a person.

modules.name: notifications
modules.description: Notifications sent by e-mail in drafting: quality managers on a new QDoc and a new version, the invitee on an invitation, and the uploader when an attachment was removed after a failed scan. Sent after the change commits.

People are assigned afresh for every version. Its reviewed marks and approvals are held by its VersionReview in the approval module.

properties.name: assignments

buildingBlocks.name: QDoc
buildingBlocks.description: The quality document as one aggregate: its versions (entities), each version's invitations and assignments, and each version's references to its content files and to its attachments. The files themselves are not part of it: content files, with their history, comments and lock, are ContentFile aggregates in content management; attachments, with their quarantine and scan, are Attachment aggregates in the file store. The root checks every drafting invariant synchronously in one transaction. The whole aggregate is saved under optimistic concurrency (concurrencyVersion): two commands that changed the same QDoc from the same starting point cannot both commit; the loser is rejected and retried on fresh state. Editing and commenting do not touch it, so they never contend with invitations or with each other across files. QDoc owns the consequences of approval that concern the version: the lock that keeps an approved attachment in it and the APPROVED status, both set by the approval module in the same transaction. Every change raises a QDoc event the activity list records.

buildingBlocks.name: QDocRepository
buildingBlocks.description: Stores and loads whole QDoc aggregates. Saving checks the concurrencyVersion the aggregate was loaded with and rejects the save when another transaction saved the QDoc in between.

buildingBlocks.name: QDocDraftingService
buildingBlocks.description: The drafting use cases. Each command loads one QDoc, looks up the acting user in the user directory, calls one method of the QDoc root, and saves the aggregate under optimistic concurrency. Adding a content file or creating a QDoc or a version also creates the content files in content management, and adding an attachment first stores it in the file store; the QDoc and the new files are saved in one transaction. The events go synchronously to the activity list in the same transaction, and after commit to notifications. A concurrency conflict is answered as such; the client reloads and retries.

buildingBlocks.name: QDocVersionAccess

properties.name: performedBy

buildingBlocks.name: VersionUnderReview

buildingBlocks.name: VersionReview
buildingBlocks.description: The review of one version of a QDoc: the reviewers' reviewed marks and the approvers' approvals of its content files and of its attachments. Identified by the QDoc and the version number; opened empty the first time anyone marks or approves on the version. It checks every approval rule against the VersionUnderReview it is given, and raises VersionApproved when the last assigned approver approves the last file. Saved under optimistic concurrency of its own.

properties.name: reviewedMarks
properties.description: The reviewers who marked the version as reviewed.

properties.name: contentFileApprovals

properties.name: attachmentApprovals

properties.name: concurrencyVersion

rules.name: Only a version in preparation is reviewed

rules.name: One review per version

rules.name: Only an assigned approver approves a shared version

buildingBlocks.name: VersionReviewRepository
buildingBlocks.description: Stores and loads VersionReview aggregates by QDoc and version number. Saving checks the concurrencyVersion the review was loaded with.

buildingBlocks.name: ApprovalService
buildingBlocks.description: The review and approval use cases. Each command loads the QDoc through the QDocRepository, the version's content files through the ContentFileRepository, its attachments through the AttachmentRepository and the version's VersionReview; looks up the acting user in the user directory; builds a VersionUnderReview; calls one method of the VersionReview and saves it. Approving a content file also locks it in content management, approving an attachment locks it on the version in the QDoc, and the last approval records the approval in the QDoc; every aggregate changed is saved in one transaction, each under its own optimistic concurrency. The events go synchronously to the activity list in the same transaction.

buildingBlocks.name: ContentFile
buildingBlocks.description: A content file of one version of a QDoc: the rich-text body the authors write, its revision, raised on every change, its change history within the version, the comments on its fragments and the lock set when an approver approved it. Saved under optimistic concurrency of its own, so two authors editing the same file contend, and edits of different files never do. Copied into a new content file for each new version.

properties.name: title
properties.description: The file's title within the version.

properties.name: revision

properties.name: history

properties.name: locked
properties.description: True once any approver approved the file; its content can no longer change and it can no longer be removed from its version.

properties.name: discarded
properties.description: True once an author removed it from its version.

properties.name: concurrencyVersion
properties.description: Optimistic-concurrency token, raised on every save.

rules.name: Every change needs access

rules.name: Approved content is locked
rules.description: Once any approver approved the file, its content can no longer be edited and the file can no longer be discarded, so no edit can ever invalidate an earlier approval. Comments stay possible. The lock is absolute in this design; a late correction between approval and publication is left to a later change.

properties.name: qDocId
properties.description: The QDoc it was uploaded for.

properties.name: performedBy
properties.description: The person or the system who did it.

buildingBlocks.name: AttachmentActivated
buildingBlocks.description: An attachment passed its scan and became active; performed by the system.

buildingBlocks.name: AttachmentRejected
buildingBlocks.description: An attachment failed its scan and was rejected; performed by the system. Drafting removes it from the version.

buildingBlocks.name: AttachmentScanner
buildingBlocks.description: Port to the scanning tool that checks an uploaded PDF for malware and unacceptable content (such as offensive images). Scanning is expected to finish within a few minutes of upload; the tool is chosen after research.

buildingBlocks.name: AttachmentRepository
buildingBlocks.description: Stores and loads attachments.

buildingBlocks.name: FileStoreService
buildingBlocks.description: The file store's use cases: storing an uploaded attachment in quarantine and requesting its scan, turning the scanner's verdict into an active or rejected attachment, and handing out download links. The verdict arrives asynchronously and is retried on failure, since it has no user to retry for it.

buildingBlocks.name: DocumentNumber
buildingBlocks.description: The human-facing document number (signature) of a QDoc, used for searching and in conversation; not a security device.

properties.name: sequence
properties.description: The position of the document among those created by its organisation in that month, from 1.

properties.name: prefix
properties.description: Everything placed before the core: the demo prefix and the organisation's prefix.

properties.name: suffix
properties.description: Everything placed after the core: the organisation's suffix and the auditor suffix.

rules.name: The core number is sequence, month and year
rules.description: The core is `<sequence>/<month>/<year>` with the month and year of creation, without leading zeros, like invoice numbering; the first document of December 2025 is 1/12/2025.

buildingBlocks.name: NumberTemplate
buildingBlocks.description: An organisation's configuration of its document numbers: a fixed prefix and a fixed suffix placed around the core template, so document numbers do not collide with, say, invoice numbers. Both are empty by default.

rules.name: Only a fixed prefix and suffix are customised
rules.description: An organisation customises only a fixed text prefix and suffix; the core `<sequence>/<month>/<year>` cannot be changed, and prefix and suffix contain no whitespace at their ends.

buildingBlocks.name: MonthlySequence
buildingBlocks.description: The running sequence of document numbers of one organisation in one month. Issued numbers are never reused; saving under optimistic concurrency stops two QDocs created at once from taking the same number.

properties.name: lastIssued
properties.description: The last sequence number issued; 0 before the first.

rules.name: The sequence restarts every month per organisation
rules.description: Each organisation has its own sequence per calendar month; the first document of a month gets 1, each next one the previous plus one, with no number issued twice.

scenarios.name: New month restarts the sequence
scenarios.description: New month restarts the sequence

scenarios.name: Organisations do not share a sequence
scenarios.description: Organisations do not share a sequence
scenarios.given: organisation A has issued 5 in December 2025 and organisation B none
scenarios.when: organisation B creates a document in December 2025
scenarios.then: it gets sequence 1

buildingBlocks.name: MonthlySequenceRepository
buildingBlocks.description: Stores and loads monthly sequences, with optimistic concurrency.

buildingBlocks.name: NumberTemplateRepository
buildingBlocks.description: Stores each organisation's number template.

buildingBlocks.name: DocumentNumberGenerator
buildingBlocks.description: Generates the document number of a new QDoc from the organisation's template, its monthly sequence, whether this instance is a demo, and whether the creator acts as auditor. Configured per deployment with the demo flag and the auditor suffix text.

properties.name: demoInstance
properties.description: True in a demo installation of the product.

properties.name: auditorSuffix
properties.description: The suffix marking a document created by an auditor as non-binding, -audit by default.

buildingBlocks.name: NumberingService
buildingBlocks.description: Configuration of an organisation's document numbers.

buildingBlocks.name: ActivityEntry
buildingBlocks.description: One line of a QDoc's activity list: what happened, to which version and content file or attachment, when, and who did it, a person or the system.

properties.name: contentFileId
properties.description: The content file concerned, if any.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: What happened: the name of the QDoc event it records.

properties.name: summary
properties.description: A readable account, e.g. who was assigned to which role by whom.

buildingBlocks.name: ActivityLog
buildingBlocks.description: The append-only store of activity entries; entries are never changed or deleted.

buildingBlocks.name: ActivityRecorder
buildingBlocks.description: Keeps the activity list of every QDoc, from the events of drafting, approval, content management and the file store, each recorded in the same transaction as the change that raised it.

rules.name: Nothing happens to a QDoc without a trace
rules.description: Every event of drafting, approval, content management and the file store leaves an activity entry: creation, every invitation and assignment (who, by whom, when) and every refusal, every content change, every comment and closing, every mark as reviewed, every approval, every file added or removed, every version created, every status change and every action by the system, such as an attachment activated, rejected or removed after its scan.

scenarios.name: Assignment appears in the activity list
scenarios.description: Assignment appears in the activity list
scenarios.given: a quality manager invited a colleague as author on 5 May
scenarios.when: the colleague accepts on 6 May
scenarios.then: the activity list shows the colleague assigned as author by that quality manager on 6 May

buildingBlocks.name: EmailMessage
buildingBlocks.description: An e-mail to one recipient.

buildingBlocks.name: EmailSender
buildingBlocks.description: Port to the e-mail delivery service.

buildingBlocks.name: QDocNotifier
buildingBlocks.description: Sends the drafting notifications by e-mail, after the change that triggered them committed. A failed send never undoes the change.

behaviours.name: findUser
behaviours.description: Answers the current snapshot of a user: roles, active flag, organisation and e-mail. Answers nothing when the user does not exist, which the invitation check treats as a refusal.

behaviours.name: findQualityManagers
behaviours.description: Answers every active user holding the quality manager role in an organisation, for the notifications on a new QDoc or version.

behaviours.name: findById
behaviours.description: Loads a whole QDoc with its concurrencyVersion.

behaviours.name: findByNumber
behaviours.description: Loads the QDoc with a given document number within an organisation, for searching by number.

behaviours.name: findWithPendingInvitationsFor
behaviours.description: Loads the QDocs that hold a pending invitation for a person.

behaviours.name: save
behaviours.description: Saves a whole QDoc if its stored concurrencyVersion still equals the one it was loaded with, and raises it by one; otherwise fails with a concurrency conflict and saves nothing.

rules.name: A stale QDoc is never saved
rules.description: A save based on an older concurrencyVersion than the stored one fails and changes nothing.

scenarios.name: Two changes to the same QDoc at once
scenarios.description: Two changes to the same QDoc at once
scenarios.given: the quality manager and an author loaded the QDoc at concurrencyVersion 7
scenarios.when: the quality manager invites a reviewer while the author adds an attachment
scenarios.then: the first save commits and raises it to 8, the second fails with a conflict and is retried on the new state

behaviours.name: create
behaviours.description: Creates a QDoc with the number already generated: status ACTIVE, version 1 with status NEW, not shared, referencing the one empty content file the drafting service created in content management, and a pending invitation for every author, reviewer and approver given. Raises QDocCreated and one InvitationSent per invitation.

rules.name: A QDoc is created by a quality manager or an auditor
rules.description: Only a user holding the quality manager or the auditor role creates a QDoc; an auditor's QDoc is marked as created by an auditor.

scenarios.name: An author cannot create a QDoc
scenarios.description: An author cannot create a QDoc
scenarios.given: a user holding only the author role
scenarios.when: they try to create a QDoc
scenarios.then: the creation is refused

rules.name: A new QDoc has a title, a type and at least one author
rules.description: A title and a document type are required and at least one author is invited at creation; reviewers and approvers are optional and can be invited later.

scenarios.name: Creating without an author is refused
scenarios.description: Creating without an author is refused
scenarios.given: a quality manager
scenarios.when: they create a QDoc with a title and a type but no author
scenarios.then: the creation is refused

scenarios.name: Creating a QDoc starts version 1
scenarios.description: Creating a QDoc starts version 1
scenarios.given: a quality manager
scenarios.when: they create a procedure with one author
scenarios.then: the QDoc has version 1 with status NEW, one empty content file and a pending author invitation, visible only to the quality manager and the invited author once accepted

behaviours.name: invite
behaviours.description: Sends an invitation to a person for a role on the version in preparation. Checks only that the inviter may invite on this QDoc, that the QDoc is not archived and that the person has no pending invitation or assignment for that role on the version; whether the person exists, holds the role and is active is checked when they accept. Raises InvitationSent.

rules.name: Only the quality manager or the auditor on own document invites
rules.description: The inviter holds the quality manager role, or holds the auditor role and created this QDoc. An author who wants a colleague asks the quality manager outside the system.

scenarios.name: An author cannot invite a colleague
scenarios.description: An author cannot invite a colleague
scenarios.given: an author assigned to a version
scenarios.when: the author invites a colleague as author
scenarios.then: the invitation is refused

scenarios.name: An auditor cannot invite on someone else's document
scenarios.description: An auditor cannot invite on someone else's document
scenarios.given: an auditor and a QDoc created by a quality manager
scenarios.when: the auditor invites a reviewer to it
scenarios.then: the invitation is refused

rules.name: One invitation per person and role on a version
rules.description: A person has at most one pending invitation or assignment for a given role on a version; the same person may hold different roles on it.

behaviours.name: acceptInvitation
behaviours.description: Accepts a pending invitation on behalf of the invitee and runs every assignment check against the current state: the inviter still holds the quality manager role (or the auditor role on their own document) and is active, the invitee exists, holds the role and is active, the QDoc is not archived and the version is still NEW. When all hold, the invitation becomes ACCEPTED and the person is added to the version's assignments for that role (InvitationAccepted). When any fails, the invitation becomes REFUSED with the failed check as reason, no assignment is made (InvitationRefused), and the call still succeeds so the refusal is recorded.

rules.name: Assignment checks run at acceptance
rules.description: An invitation turns into an assignment only if, at the moment of acceptance, the inviter is a quality manager or the auditor on their own document, the invitee exists, holds the role invited to and is active, the QDoc is not archived and the version is still in preparation. Otherwise the assignment is refused.

scenarios.name: Accepting with the role held is assigned
scenarios.description: Accepting with the role held is assigned
scenarios.given: an invitation to be author of version 1, and the invitee is active and holds the author role
scenarios.when: the invitee accepts
scenarios.then: the invitee appears on version 1's authors, and the activity list shows who was assigned, by whom and when

scenarios.name: Role withdrawn before acceptance is refused
scenarios.description: Role withdrawn before acceptance is refused
scenarios.given: an invitation to be reviewer, and the invitee's reviewer role was withdrawn after the invitation was sent
scenarios.when: the invitee accepts
scenarios.then: the invitation is refused, the invitee is not a reviewer, and the refusal appears in the activity list

scenarios.name: Deactivated invitee is refused
scenarios.description: Deactivated invitee is refused
scenarios.given: an invitation to be approver for a person whose account was blocked since
scenarios.when: the acceptance is attempted
scenarios.then: the invitation is refused and no approver is added

scenarios.name: Replacement for a reviewer who left
scenarios.description: Replacement for a reviewer who left
scenarios.given: version 2 pre-filled with version 1's reviewers, one of whom has left the company and is deactivated
scenarios.when: the quality manager invites the old reviewers and a replacement, and the invitees accept
scenarios.then: the one who left is refused and the replacement is assigned

rules.name: Only the invitee accepts an invitation
rules.description: An invitation is accepted by the person it was sent to and by nobody else.

behaviours.name: createNewVersion
behaviours.description: Creates the next version after the latest one was published: status NEW, not shared, referencing the copies of the previous version's content files the drafting service made in content management and the same stored attachments as the previous version, no locked attachments and no people. Reviewed marks and approvals are not copied: the new version gets a VersionReview of its own in the approval module. Raises NewVersionCreated.

rules.name: New version only after the previous one is published
rules.description: A new version is created only by the quality manager or the auditor on own document, only when the latest version has been published (status PUBLISHED or RETIRED) and the QDoc is not archived.

scenarios.name: New version while one is approved but unpublished is refused
scenarios.description: New version while one is approved but unpublished is refused
scenarios.given: a QDoc whose latest version is APPROVED
scenarios.when: the quality manager creates a new version
scenarios.then: the creation is refused

scenarios.name: Later change
scenarios.description: Later change
scenarios.given: a QDoc numbered 1/12/2025 whose version 1 is PUBLISHED
scenarios.when: the quality manager creates version 2
scenarios.then: version 2 is NEW with a copy of version 1's files, version 1 stays the one in force, and every quality manager is notified

rules.name: A new version starts as a full copy with no people
rules.description: The new version contains every file of the previous one: each content file copied into a new content file with a fresh history, and every attachment referenced as it is, since attachments never change. It starts with no invitations and no assignments: authors, reviewers and approvers are invited afresh. The number of files may then diverge.

behaviours.name: addContentFile
behaviours.description: Adds to the version in preparation a reference to a new, empty content file created in content management. Raises ContentFileAdded.

rules.name: Only authors change the version's files
rules.description: Only a person assigned as author of the version adds, edits or removes its files; quality managers, reviewers and approvers never do.

scenarios.name: A reviewer cannot add a file
scenarios.description: A reviewer cannot add a file
scenarios.given: a reviewer assigned to a shared version
scenarios.when: the reviewer adds a content file
scenarios.then: the change is refused

behaviours.name: addAttachment
behaviours.description: Adds to the version in preparation a reference to an attachment just stored, in quarantine, in the file store. Raises AttachmentAdded.

behaviours.name: removeRejectedAttachment
behaviours.description: Removes from the version in preparation an attachment the file store rejected after a failed scan, as an action of the system, and raises AttachmentRemovedAfterFailedScan with the findings and the uploader, so the activity list records it and the uploader is e-mailed. Ignored when the attachment is no longer on the version.

rules.name: A failed attachment is removed by the system
rules.description: An attachment whose scan failed never becomes active: the system removes it from the version, records the removal as a system action and the uploading author is e-mailed what was found and that the file was removed.

scenarios.name: Suspicious attachment
scenarios.description: Suspicious attachment
scenarios.given: an author uploaded a PDF that fails the malware check
scenarios.when: the scan result arrives
scenarios.then: the file never became downloadable or approvable, it is removed from the version, the activity list shows the removal by the system, and the author receives an e-mail explaining what was found

behaviours.name: removeContentFile
behaviours.description: Removes the reference to a content file from the version in preparation, as long as another content file remains. The drafting service discards the content file in content management in the same transaction, which refuses when an approval locked it. Raises ContentFileRemoved.

behaviours.name: removeAttachment
behaviours.description: Removes the reference to an attachment from the version in preparation, unless an approver approved it on this version. The stored attachment stays in the file store, since earlier versions may still refer to it. Raises AttachmentRemoved.

behaviours.name: shareVersion
behaviours.description: Shares the version in preparation with its reviewers and approvers: sets sharedForReview. From then on they see it and may comment. The authors keep editing. Raises VersionShared.

rules.name: Sharing needs at least one approver
rules.description: A version is shared only by one of its authors, only once, and only when at least one approver is assigned (an accepted invitation, not a pending one). Reviewers are optional.

scenarios.name: Sharing without an approver is refused
scenarios.description: Sharing without an approver is refused
scenarios.given: a version with one author and two reviewers, and an approver invitation still pending
scenarios.when: the author shares the version
scenarios.then: the sharing is refused

scenarios.name: Sharing with one approver and no reviewers
scenarios.description: Sharing with one approver and no reviewers
scenarios.given: a version with one assigned author and one assigned approver
scenarios.when: the author shares it
scenarios.then: the version is flagged as shared and the approver can now see and comment on it

behaviours.name: lockAttachment
behaviours.description: Locks an attachment on the version in preparation because an approver approved it, so it can no longer be removed from the version. Called by the approval module in the same transaction as the approval. Locking an already locked attachment changes nothing.

behaviours.name: recordApproval
behaviours.description: Records that every assigned approver approved every content file and every attachment of the version in preparation: the version becomes APPROVED with approvedAt. Called by the approval module in the same transaction as the last approval; the VersionApproved event it answers to is raised by the VersionReview.

rules.name: Only a version in preparation becomes approved
rules.description: Only the version with status NEW becomes APPROVED.

behaviours.name: markPublished
behaviours.description: Records that the publication part published the approved version: it becomes PUBLISHED and the version published before, if any, becomes RETIRED. Raises VersionPublished. Publication itself is out of scope.

rules.name: Only an approved version is published
rules.description: Only the version with status APPROVED becomes PUBLISHED; publishing it retires the version in force before it.

behaviours.name: markWithdrawn
behaviours.description: Records that the publication part withdrew the published version from force without a successor: it becomes RETIRED. Raises VersionWithdrawn. How withdrawal happens is out of scope.

behaviours.name: archive
behaviours.description: Archives the QDoc so it stops cluttering people's lists. Raises QDocArchived.

rules.name: Archive only without a version in force or in preparation
rules.description: A QDoc is archived by the quality manager or the auditor on own document, only when none of its versions is NEW, APPROVED or PUBLISHED.

scenarios.name: Archiving with a version in preparation is refused
scenarios.description: Archiving with a version in preparation is refused
scenarios.given: a QDoc whose version 2 is NEW
scenarios.when: the quality manager archives it
scenarios.then: the archiving is refused

scenarios.name: Archiving a withdrawn QDoc
scenarios.description: Archiving a withdrawn QDoc
scenarios.given: a QDoc whose only version was withdrawn from force
scenarios.when: the quality manager archives it
scenarios.then: the QDoc is ARCHIVED and accepts no further invitations or versions

behaviours.name: createQDoc
behaviours.description: Creates a QDoc. Input: the acting user and CreateQDoc. Looks up the creator, has the numbering module generate the document number (auditor suffix when the creator is an auditor, demo prefix in a demo instance), creates the first, empty content file in content management, calls QDoc.create with it and saves both. Output: the new QDoc's id. Every other quality manager of the organisation is notified after commit.

scenarios.name: Audit test document
scenarios.description: Audit test document
scenarios.given: an external auditor
scenarios.when: the auditor creates a test procedure and invites a member of the audited team as author and approver
scenarios.then: its number carries the auditor suffix and the document goes through drafting like any other; the system does not hide it

behaviours.name: inviteToVersion
behaviours.description:
Invites a person to a role on the QDoc's version in preparation, also used to invite people to a new version (the form may pre-fill the previous version's people). Output: the invitation id; the invitee is notified after commit.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Quality manager->>QDocDraftingService: inviteToVersion(userId, qdocId, invitee, role)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: findById(qdocId)
  QDocDraftingService->>UserDirectory: findUser(userId)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDoc: invite(inviter, invitee, role, now)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: save(qdoc)
  QDocDraftingService-->>QDocNotifier: after commit: InvitationSent
```

scenarios.name: Second author
scenarios.description: Second author
scenarios.given: an author asked the quality manager outside the system to add a colleague who holds the author role and is active
scenarios.when: the quality manager invites the colleague as author and the colleague accepts
scenarios.then: the colleague is an author of the version and the activity list shows the assignment with its date and the quality manager's name

behaviours.name: acceptInvitation
behaviours.description:
The invitee accepts an invitation. Looks up both the invitee and the inviter in the user directory now, and has the QDoc run every assignment check. Output: whether the assignment was made; a refusal is recorded and reported, not thrown, since it mostly comes from misuse or a role withdrawn in between.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Author->>QDocDraftingService: acceptInvitation(userId, qdocId, invitationId)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: findById(qdocId)
  QDocDraftingService->>UserDirectory: findUser(invitee)
  QDocDraftingService->>UserDirectory: findUser(inviter)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDoc: acceptInvitation(invitationId, invitee, inviter, now)
  QDoc-->>QDocDraftingService: InvitationAccepted or InvitationRefused
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: save(qdoc)
```

behaviours.name: getMyInvitations
behaviours.description: Lists the pending invitations of the acting user, with the QDoc's number, title, version and role.

behaviours.name: createNewVersion
behaviours.description:
Creates the next version of a published QDoc: copies each content file of the previous version into a new content file in content management, then has the QDoc create the version referencing the copies and the previous version's attachments; the QDoc and the copies are saved in one transaction. Output: the new version number. Every quality manager is notified after commit.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Quality manager->>QDocDraftingService: createNewVersion(userId, qdocId)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: findById(qdocId)
  QDocDraftingService->>ContentFileRepository: findForVersion(qdocId, previousVersion)
  QDocDraftingService->>ContentFile: copyForVersion(newId, newVersion, now)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDoc: createNewVersion(actor, copyIds, now)
  QDocDraftingService->>ContentFileRepository: save(copies)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: save(qdoc)
  QDocDraftingService-->>QDocNotifier: after commit: NewVersionCreated
```

behaviours.name: addContentFile
behaviours.description:
Adds an empty content file to the version in preparation: creates it in content management and references it from the version, saving both in one transaction. Output: the new content file's id.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Author->>QDocDraftingService: addContentFile(userId, qdocId, title)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: findById(qdocId)
  QDocDraftingService->>ContentFile: create(newId, qdocId, organisationId, versionNumber, title, now)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDoc: addContentFile(actor, newId, title, now)
  QDocDraftingService->>ContentFileRepository: save(contentFile)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: save(qdoc)
```

behaviours.name: addAttachment
behaviours.description:
Adds an uploaded PDF to the version in preparation: the binary is stored first and referred to by its storage key, the file store records it as a quarantined attachment and has it scanned, and the version references it; all in one transaction. Output: the new attachment's id.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Author->>QDocDraftingService: addAttachment(userId, qdocId, fileName, storageKey)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: findById(qdocId)
  QDocDraftingService->>FileStoreService: storeAttachment(qdocId, organisationId, userId, fileName, storageKey)
  FileStoreService-->>QDocDraftingService: attachmentId
  QDocDraftingService->>QDoc: addAttachment(actor, attachmentId, fileName, now)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: save(qdoc)
```

behaviours.name: removeContentFile
behaviours.description:
Removes a content file from the version in preparation: the QDoc drops its reference and content management discards the file, in one transaction.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Author->>QDocDraftingService: removeContentFile(userId, qdocId, contentFileId)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: findById(qdocId)
  QDocDraftingService->>ContentFileRepository: findById(contentFileId)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDoc: removeContentFile(actor, contentFileId, now)
  QDocDraftingService->>ContentFile: discard(now)
  QDocDraftingService->>ContentFileRepository: save(contentFile)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: save(qdoc)
```

behaviours.name: removeAttachment
behaviours.description:
Removes an attachment from the version in preparation.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Author->>QDocDraftingService: removeAttachment(userId, qdocId, attachmentId)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: findById(qdocId)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDoc: removeAttachment(actor, attachmentId, now)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: save(qdoc)
```

behaviours.name: shareVersion
behaviours.description:
Shares the version in preparation with its reviewers and approvers.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Author->>QDocDraftingService: shareVersion(userId, qdocId)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: findById(qdocId)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDoc: shareVersion(actor, now)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: save(qdoc)
```

behaviours.name: archiveQDoc
behaviours.description:
Archives a QDoc with no version in force or in preparation.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Quality manager->>QDocDraftingService: archiveQDoc(userId, qdocId)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: findById(qdocId)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDoc: archive(actor, now)
  QDocDraftingService->>QDocRepository: save(qdoc)
```

behaviours.name: onAttachmentRejected
behaviours.description: Reacts to the file store rejecting an attachment after a failed scan: has the system remove it from the version that references it. Retried on a concurrency conflict, since it has no user to retry for it.

behaviours.name: recordPublication
behaviours.description: Entry point for the publication part of the system, out of scope here: it reports that it published an approved version. Marks it PUBLISHED and retires the one in force before it.

behaviours.name: recordWithdrawal
behaviours.description: Entry point for the publication part: it reports that it withdrew a published version from force without a successor. Marks it RETIRED, which is what later allows archiving.

behaviours.name: getVersion
behaviours.description: Answers a version of a QDoc with its references to content files and attachments, its locked attachments and its people, for a member of its drafting team. The content files come from ContentService.getContentFile, the attachments' status from the file store, and the reviewed marks and approvals from ApprovalService.getReview.

rules.name: Drafts are visible to the drafting team only
rules.description: Before sharing, a version is visible to the quality manager who created the QDoc (or the auditor who did) and to its assigned authors; after sharing also to its assigned reviewers and approvers. Pending invitees and employees never see a draft; employees see only the published version, through the publication part.

scenarios.description: Reviewer before sharing sees nothing
scenarios.given: a reviewer assigned to a version not yet shared
scenarios.when: the reviewer opens the version
scenarios.then: access is refused

scenarios.name: Reviewer after sharing sees the version
scenarios.description: Reviewer after sharing sees the version

scenarios.then: the version is shown

behaviours.name: downloadAttachment
behaviours.description: Answers a short-lived download link to an attachment of the version, from the file store, for a member of the drafting team who can see the version.

behaviours.name: accessFor
behaviours.description: Answers what a person may do with the content of a version: loads the QDoc and computes the ContentAccess from the version's status, shared flag and assignments.

rules.name: Only authors edit content
rules.description: A person may edit the content files of a version only while it is NEW and only as one of its assigned authors; quality managers, reviewers and approvers never edit.

rules.name: Comments come from the drafting team
rules.description: The quality manager who created the QDoc, the auditor on own document and the version's authors may comment at any time while it is in preparation; its reviewers and approvers only after it was shared.

scenarios.name: Reviewer cannot comment before sharing
scenarios.description: Reviewer cannot comment before sharing
scenarios.given: a reviewer assigned to a version not yet shared
scenarios.when: the reviewer comments
scenarios.then: the comment is refused

rules.name: Only an approver closes comments
rules.description: Only a person assigned as approver of the shared version may close a comment; closing acknowledges it was seen, whether or not it led to a change.

rules.name: Content is seen by whoever sees the version
rules.description: A person may see the content files, their history and their comments exactly when they may see the version: before sharing the creator and the authors, after sharing also the reviewers and approvers. Pending invitees and employees never.

behaviours.name: markReviewed
behaviours.description: Records that a reviewer read the shared version and has no objections. Informational only: nothing waits for it. Raises VersionMarkedReviewed.

rules.name: Only a reviewer marks a shared version as reviewed
rules.description: A person assigned as reviewer marks a shared version as reviewed, once. A reviewer who says nothing is treated as silently accepting.

behaviours.name: approveContentFile
behaviours.description: Records an approver's approval of one content file at the revision the approver saw and raises ContentFileApproved; when every assigned approver has now approved every current file of the version, also raises VersionApproved. The ApprovalService then locks the content file and, on VersionApproved, records the approval in the QDoc, in the same transaction.

rules.name: No open comments on an approved content file
rules.description: A content file is approved only when none of its comments is open; the approver must close every comment first.

scenarios.name: Approval attempt with open comments
scenarios.description: Approval attempt with open comments
scenarios.given: a content file with a reviewer's open comment
scenarios.when: the approver approves the file
scenarios.then: the approval is refused; after the approver closes the comment, the same approval goes through

rules.name: Approval applies to the content the approver saw
rules.description: The approval names the file revision the approver looked at; if the file's current revision differs, the approval does not go through.

scenarios.name: Content changed under the approver
scenarios.description: Content changed under the approver
scenarios.given: an approver opened a content file at revision 3 and an author then saved revision 4
scenarios.when: the approver approves revision 3
scenarios.then: the approval is refused and the approver must look at revision 4

behaviours.name: approveAttachment
behaviours.description: Records an approver's approval of one attachment and raises AttachmentApproved; when every assigned approver has now approved every current file of the version, also raises VersionApproved. The ApprovalService then locks the attachment on the version and, on VersionApproved, records the approval in the QDoc, in the same transaction.

rules.name: Only active attachments are approved
rules.description: An attachment still in quarantine cannot be approved.

scenarios.name: Approving a quarantined attachment is refused
scenarios.description: Approving a quarantined attachment is refused
scenarios.given: a shared version with an attachment still being scanned
scenarios.when: the approver approves the attachment
scenarios.then: the approval is refused

behaviours.name: findOrOpen
behaviours.description: Loads the review of a version, or answers a new, empty one when nobody has reviewed the version yet.

behaviours.name: save
behaviours.description: Saves a review if its stored concurrencyVersion still equals the one it was loaded with, and raises it by one; otherwise fails with a concurrency conflict and saves nothing.

rules.name: A stale review is never saved
rules.description: A save based on an older concurrencyVersion than the stored one fails and changes nothing.

behaviours.name: markVersionReviewed
behaviours.description:
Marks the shared version as reviewed by the acting reviewer.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Reviewer->>ApprovalService: markVersionReviewed(userId, qdocId)
  ApprovalService->>QDocRepository: findById(qdocId)
  ApprovalService->>VersionReviewRepository: findOrOpen(qdocId, versionNumber)
  ApprovalService->>VersionReview: markReviewed(actor, versionUnderReview, now)
  ApprovalService->>VersionReviewRepository: save(review)
```

behaviours.name: approveContentFile
behaviours.description:
Approves one content file at the revision the approver saw. Output: the version's status after the approval, APPROVED when this was the last approval. The review, the content file and, on the last approval, the QDoc are saved in one transaction; a concurrent edit of the file makes either the revision check or the content file's save fail, and nothing is approved.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Approver->>ApprovalService: approveContentFile(userId, qdocId, contentFileId, seenRevision)
  ApprovalService->>QDocRepository: findById(qdocId)
  ApprovalService->>ContentFileRepository: findForVersion(qdocId, versionNumber)
  ApprovalService->>AttachmentRepository: findById(each attachment of the version)
  ApprovalService->>VersionReviewRepository: findOrOpen(qdocId, versionNumber)
  ApprovalService->>VersionReview: approveContentFile(actor, versionUnderReview, contentFileId, seenRevision, now)
  VersionReview-->>ApprovalService: approved event, VersionApproved?
  ApprovalService->>ContentFile: lock(seenRevision)
  ApprovalService->>QDoc: recordApproval(versionNumber, now) if VersionApproved
  ApprovalService->>VersionReviewRepository: save(review)
  ApprovalService->>ContentFileRepository: save(contentFile)
  ApprovalService->>QDocRepository: save(qdoc) if VersionApproved
  ApprovalService->>ActivityRecorder: onQDocEvent(events)
```

behaviours.name: approveAttachment
behaviours.description:
Approves one attachment of the version. Output: the version's status after the approval, APPROVED when this was the last approval. The review and the QDoc are saved in one transaction.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Approver->>ApprovalService: approveAttachment(userId, qdocId, attachmentId)
  ApprovalService->>QDocRepository: findById(qdocId)
  ApprovalService->>ContentFileRepository: findForVersion(qdocId, versionNumber)
  ApprovalService->>AttachmentRepository: findById(each attachment of the version)
  ApprovalService->>VersionReviewRepository: findOrOpen(qdocId, versionNumber)
  ApprovalService->>VersionReview: approveAttachment(actor, versionUnderReview, attachmentId, now)
  VersionReview-->>ApprovalService: approved event, VersionApproved?
  ApprovalService->>QDoc: lockAttachment(versionNumber, attachmentId)
  ApprovalService->>QDoc: recordApproval(versionNumber, now) if VersionApproved
  ApprovalService->>VersionReviewRepository: save(review)
  ApprovalService->>QDocRepository: save(qdoc)
  ApprovalService->>ActivityRecorder: onQDocEvent(events)
```

behaviours.name: getReview
behaviours.description: Answers the review of a version: its reviewed marks and its approvals of content files and attachments, for a member of its drafting team. Comments come with the content file from ContentService.getContentFile.

rules.name: A review is visible to whoever sees the version
rules.description: The review of a version is shown to exactly the people who may see the version in drafting: before sharing the creator and the authors, after sharing also the reviewers and approvers.

scenarios.name: Reviewer before sharing sees no comments
scenarios.description: Reviewer before sharing sees no comments
scenarios.given: a reviewer assigned to a version not yet shared, on which an author left a comment
scenarios.when: the reviewer opens the version's review
scenarios.then: access is refused

behaviours.name: create
behaviours.description: Creates an empty content file with a title for a version: revision 1, no history, no comments, unlocked.

behaviours.name: copyForVersion
behaviours.description: Answers a new content file for the next version with this file's title and current body, a fresh history starting at revision 1, no comments and unlocked.

behaviours.name: edit
behaviours.description: Saves an author's edit: the new content, based on the revision the author's editor last loaded. Raises the revision by one, appends a ContentRevision to the history and raises ContentFileEdited. Editing may continue after sharing. Collaborative editing is resolved by the editor before saving; on the server a stale base revision or a stale file is rejected and the editor merges and retries.

rules.name: An edit applies to the revision it was based on
rules.description: An edit is accepted only when its base revision equals the file's current revision; otherwise it is rejected so no author silently overwrites another's change.

scenarios.name: Stale edit is rejected
scenarios.description: Stale edit is rejected
scenarios.given: a content file at revision 5 and an author whose editor loaded revision 4
scenarios.when: the author saves an edit based on revision 4
scenarios.then: the edit is rejected and the file stays at revision 5

scenarios.name: Author edits after sharing
scenarios.description: Author edits after sharing
scenarios.given: a shared version with an open comment asking for a missing section
scenarios.when: the author adds the section
scenarios.then: the file's revision rises, the edit appears in the file's history and in the activity list

behaviours.name: addComment
behaviours.description: Adds an open comment on a fragment of the content. Raises CommentAdded.

behaviours.name: closeComment
behaviours.description: Closes an open comment. Raises CommentClosed.

behaviours.name: lock
behaviours.description: Locks the file because an approver approved it at the given revision. Called by the approval module in the same transaction as the approval. Locking an already locked file changes nothing.

rules.name: Content is locked at the revision that was approved
rules.description: The lock is set only when the file's current revision equals the approved revision; otherwise the lock, and with it the approval, is refused.

scenarios.name: Lock after a concurrent edit is refused
scenarios.description: Lock after a concurrent edit is refused
scenarios.given: an approver approved revision 3 of a content file, and an author saved revision 4 in between
scenarios.when: the approval module locks the file at revision 3
scenarios.then: the lock is refused, the whole approval rolls back and the approver must look at revision 4

behaviours.name: discard
behaviours.description: Marks the file removed from its version, when drafting removes its reference. Refused when an approval locked it.

behaviours.name: findById
behaviours.description: Loads a content file with its concurrencyVersion.

behaviours.name: findForVersion
behaviours.description: Loads the content files of a version that were not discarded.

behaviours.name: save
behaviours.description: Saves a content file if its stored concurrencyVersion still equals the one it was loaded with, and raises it by one; otherwise fails with a concurrency conflict and saves nothing.

rules.name: A stale content file is never saved
rules.description: A save based on an older concurrencyVersion than the stored one fails and changes nothing.

scenarios.name: Two authors save edits to the same content file at once
scenarios.description: Two authors save edits to the same content file at once
scenarios.given: two authors loaded the same content file at concurrencyVersion 7
scenarios.when: both save an edit
scenarios.then: the first save commits and raises it to 8, the second fails with a conflict and its author's editor reloads and retries on the new state

behaviours.name: accessFor
behaviours.description: Answers what a person may do with the content of a version.

behaviours.name: editContentFile
behaviours.description:
Saves an edit of a content file based on the revision the author's editor loaded. Output: the new revision. A conflict (stale revision or stale file) is answered as such so the editor merges and retries; only authors editing the same file contend.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram

  ContentService->>VersionAccess: accessFor(userId, qdocId, versionNumber)
  ContentService->>ContentFile: edit(actor, access, baseRevision, content, now)
  ContentService->>ContentFileRepository: save(contentFile)
```

behaviours.name: addComment
behaviours.description:
Leaves a comment on a fragment of a content file. Output: the comment id.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Reviewer->>ContentService: addComment(userId, contentFileId, fragment, text)
  ContentService->>ContentFileRepository: findById(contentFileId)
  ContentService->>VersionAccess: accessFor(userId, qdocId, versionNumber)
  ContentService->>ContentFile: addComment(actor, access, fragment, text, now)
  ContentService->>ContentFileRepository: save(contentFile)
```

behaviours.name: closeComment
behaviours.description:
Closes an open comment on a content file.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  Approver->>ContentService: closeComment(userId, contentFileId, commentId)
  ContentService->>ContentFileRepository: findById(contentFileId)
  ContentService->>VersionAccess: accessFor(userId, qdocId, versionNumber)
  ContentService->>ContentFile: closeComment(actor, access, commentId, now)

```

behaviours.name: getContentFile
behaviours.description: Answers a content file with its current content, revision, lock and comments, to a person VersionAccess lets see it.

behaviours.name: getContentFileHistory
behaviours.description: Answers the change history of a content file within its version: who changed what and when, to a person VersionAccess lets see it; never to employees.

behaviours.name: upload
behaviours.description: Records an uploaded PDF as an attachment in quarantine.

behaviours.name: activate
behaviours.description: Makes a quarantined attachment ACTIVE after its scan passed. Raises AttachmentActivated, performed by the system.

behaviours.name: reject
behaviours.description: Makes a quarantined attachment REJECTED after its scan failed, keeping the findings. Raises AttachmentRejected, performed by the system.

behaviours.name: findById
behaviours.description: Loads an attachment.

behaviours.name: save
behaviours.description: Saves an attachment.

behaviours.name: requestScan
behaviours.description: Hands the stored attachment to the scanning tool; the verdict comes back asynchronously.

behaviours.name: storeAttachment
behaviours.description: Stores an uploaded PDF as a quarantined attachment of a QDoc and, after commit, requests its scan. Called by drafting when an author adds an attachment. Output: the attachment id. Size limits are undecided pending research and not checked.

rules.name: Every uploaded attachment is scanned
rules.description: Every attachment is scanned for malware and unacceptable content before it can become active.

behaviours.name: onScanFinished
behaviours.description: Receives the scanning tool's verdict and activates or rejects the attachment. Ignored when the attachment is no longer quarantined.

behaviours.name: downloadLink
behaviours.description: Answers a short-lived download link to an attachment. Called by drafting once it has checked the person may see the version.

rules.name: Only active attachments can be downloaded
rules.description: A quarantined attachment cannot be downloaded by anybody.

scenarios.name: Downloading a quarantined attachment is refused
scenarios.description: Downloading a quarantined attachment is refused
scenarios.given: an attachment uploaded a minute ago and still being scanned
scenarios.when: an approver downloads it
scenarios.then: the download is refused

behaviours.name: issueNext
behaviours.description: Raises lastIssued by one and answers it.

behaviours.name: findOrStart
behaviours.description: Loads the sequence of an organisation for a month, or a fresh one at 0 when none exists yet.

behaviours.name: save
behaviours.description: Saves a sequence; fails on a concurrent change so the number is issued again.

behaviours.name: findFor
behaviours.description: Answers the organisation's template, or an empty one when none was configured.

behaviours.name: save
behaviours.description: Stores an organisation's template.

behaviours.name: generate
behaviours.description:
Issues the next sequence number of the organisation for the month of the creation date, reads the organisation's template, and assembles the document number: demo prefix, organisation prefix, core, organisation suffix, auditor suffix when the creator holds the auditor role and acts as such. Called by drafting when a QDoc is created, in the same transaction.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  QDocDraftingService->>DocumentNumberGenerator: generate(organisationId, creatorRoles, date)
  DocumentNumberGenerator->>MonthlySequenceRepository: findOrStart(organisationId, year, month)
  DocumentNumberGenerator->>MonthlySequence: issueNext()
  DocumentNumberGenerator->>MonthlySequenceRepository: save(sequence)
  DocumentNumberGenerator->>NumberTemplateRepository: findFor(organisationId)
```

behaviours.name: configureTemplate
behaviours.description: Sets the organisation's fixed prefix and suffix. Applies to documents created afterwards; numbers already given never change.

behaviours.name: append
behaviours.description: Appends entries.

behaviours.name: findFor
behaviours.description: Answers a QDoc's entries, oldest first.

behaviours.name: onContentEvent

behaviours.name: onAttachmentEvent
behaviours.description: Turns each file store event into an activity entry of the QDoc the attachment was uploaded for, marked as an action of the system where it was, and appends it in the same transaction as the change.

behaviours.name: getActivity
behaviours.description: Answers a QDoc's activity list to someone who may see the QDoc's drafts, oldest first.

rules.name: Employees never see the activity list
rules.description: The activity list is shown to quality managers and to the authors, reviewers and approvers of the document; never to regular employees.

behaviours.name: send
